{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Go as the implementation language, consistent with the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase.",
    "Implement the Solo orderer as a standalone process exposing a gRPC interface, using a buffered Go channel for client writes and a single goroutine for batch/block creation.",
    "Use an in-memory ledger (slice of blocks) for the Solo orderer, with optional periodic snapshotting to disk for crash recovery.",
    "Implement client seek by exposing block-by-height and block-hash lookup over gRPC, allowing reconnecting clients to resume delivery.",
    "Design the state cache as an LRU-based structure integrated into the peer, exposed via an internal API for transaction simulation and rw-set building.",
    "Extract CLI commands into a separate Go module/binary that interacts with the peer/orderer only via their public gRPC APIs, removing the dependency on RocksDB and peer internals.",
    "Build CLI binaries per platform (Linux, macOS, Windows) using a cross-compilation Makefile and GitHub Actions.",
    "Implement friendly names for chaincode via a name-to-id mapping persisted in the ledger and resolved during chaincode invocation queries.",
    "Implement the lifecycle system chaincode as a regular system chaincode (similar to QSCC or CSCC) exposing deployment policy management operations.",
    "Store deployment policies (e.g., endorsement, validation policies) inside the lifecycle chaincode state, queryable by other components.",
    "Host unified documentation at hyperledger.org using a static site generator (e.g., Jekyll or Sphinx) by mirroring content from each Hyperledger project repository.",
    "Mirror the Fabric source code from Gerrit to a public GitHub repository using a sync job; documentation work is treated as deliverable artifacts rather than executable code."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single experienced Go developer familiar with Hyperledger Fabric internals performs all work.",
    "An 8-hour workday is used; estimates exclude meetings, holidays, and non-engineering overhead.",
    "Unit testing is included within each development activity (no separate test activity unless integration).",
    "Code review effort is included within each activity and not itemized separately.",
    "The existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase, build system, and CI infrastructure are available and usable as a starting point.",
    "No formal user acceptance testing (UAT) is included; only technical integration testing.",
    "Cross-platform packaging (macOS, Windows) of the CLI is included in the CLI extraction activity but not separately broken out per OS.",
    "Documentation work for U3 and U7 covers drafting, organizing, and publishing content; it is treated as software increment deliverable effort even though the output is largely textual.",
    "GitHub mirror setup (U5) is largely a configuration/scripting task and does not involve code changes beyond automation scripts.",
    "Backwards compatibility with earlier Fabric APIs is not a hard requirement, simplifying refactoring choices."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and architecture design",
      "activity_description": "Analyze all user stories, define the overall architecture for the increment, design internal APIs (state cache, lifecycle CC, friendly name resolution, CLI, Solo orderer), and produce a technical design document that guides implementation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "U1: Friendly name for chaincode",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a name-to-chaincode-id mapping mechanism, update chaincode deployment flows to accept friendly names, update chaincode invocation/lookup paths to resolve friendly names, and add unit/integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "U2: Lifecycle system chaincode for deployment policies",
      "activity_description": "Design the lifecycle system chaincode interface, implement deployment policy management operations (set/get endorsement and validation policies), persist policies in chaincode state, integrate with chaincode deployment/upgrade flows, and add unit/integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "U3: Upgrade flow documentation",
      "activity_description": "Author clear, step-by-step documentation covering chaincode upgrade flows, including prerequisites, command sequences, policy updates, and rollback considerations; publish through the documentation portal.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "U4: Solo ordering process",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Solo orderer: a minimal orderer with a buffered Go channel for client submissions, a single batch-creation goroutine producing blocks, an in-RAM ledger of recent blocks, gRPC seek/replay support for reconnecting clients, and unit/integration tests covering happy path, disconnection, and replay scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "U5: GitHub repository mirror",
      "activity_description": "Set up a public GitHub repository for Hyperledger Fabric and implement a sync script/job that mirrors commits from Gerrit to GitHub on a regular cadence, plus README and contribution notes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "U6: State cache for rw-set building",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement an LRU-based state cache within the peer, expose an internal API for transaction simulation, integrate the cache with the read-write set construction path, and add unit tests plus performance benchmarks to demonstrate the improvement.",
      "most_likely_effort": 7
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "U7: Unified documentation portal",
      "activity_description": "Stand up a unified documentation site at hyperledger.org, establish the layout for all Hyperledger projects, migrate existing Fabric documentation into the new structure, and verify links and rendering.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "U8: CLI extraction and cross-platform packaging",
      "activity_description": "Refactor peer CLI commands into a separate Go module that depends only on the peer's public gRPC API, remove RocksDB and other internal peer dependencies, build platform-specific binaries (Linux, macOS, Windows) via cross-compilation and CI, and add install/distribution instructions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "End-to-end integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Run a sample application end-to-end across the new CLI, peer with state cache, lifecycle system chaincode, friendly-name chaincodes, and the Solo orderer; validate upgrade flow and disconnect/reconnect behavior; capture results.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Defect fixing and stabilization",
      "activity_description": "Address issues found during integration testing and self-review, polish error messages, and ensure all unit/integration tests pass cleanly.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 58
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go as the implementation language, consistent with the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase.
Implement the Solo orderer as a standalone process exposing a gRPC interface, using a buffered Go channel for client writes and a single goroutine for batch/block creation.
Use an in-memory ledger (slice of blocks) for the Solo orderer, with optional periodic snapshotting to disk for crash recovery.
Implement client seek by exposing block-by-height and block-hash lookup over gRPC, allowing reconnecting clients to resume delivery.
Design the state cache as an LRU-based structure integrated into the peer, exposed via an internal API for transaction simulation and rw-set building.
Extract CLI commands into a separate Go module/binary that interacts with the peer/orderer only via their public gRPC APIs, removing the dependency on RocksDB and peer internals.
Build CLI binaries per platform (Linux, macOS, Windows) using a cross-compilation Makefile and GitHub Actions.
Implement friendly names for chaincode via a name-to-id mapping persisted in the ledger and resolved during chaincode invocation queries.
Implement the lifecycle system chaincode as a regular system chaincode (similar to QSCC or CSCC) exposing deployment policy management operations.
Store deployment policies (e.g., endorsement, validation policies) inside the lifecycle chaincode state, queryable by other components.
Host unified documentation at hyperledger.org using a static site generator (e.g., Jekyll or Sphinx) by mirroring content from each Hyperledger project repository.
Mirror the Fabric source code from Gerrit to a public GitHub repository using a sync job; documentation work is treated as deliverable artifacts rather than executable code.
assumptions: A single experienced Go developer familiar with Hyperledger Fabric internals performs all work.
An 8-hour workday is used; estimates exclude meetings, holidays, and non-engineering overhead.
Unit testing is included within each development activity (no separate test activity unless integration).
Code review effort is included within each activity and not itemized separately.
The existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase, build system, and CI infrastructure are available and usable as a starting point.
No formal user acceptance testing (UAT) is included; only technical integration testing.
Cross-platform packaging (macOS, Windows) of the CLI is included in the CLI extraction activity but not separately broken out per OS.
Documentation work for U3 and U7 covers drafting, organizing, and publishing content; it is treated as software increment deliverable effort even though the output is largely textual.
GitHub mirror setup (U5) is largely a configuration/scripting task and does not involve code changes beyond automation scripts.
Backwards compatibility with earlier Fabric APIs is not a hard requirement, simplifying refactoring choices.
